newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS USE FOUR GOALS IN FIRST PERIOD TO BEAT BRUINS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS USE FOUR GOALS IN FIRST PERIOD TO BEAT BRUINS.

text.p: Joel Otto and Eric Lindros scored 19 seconds apart to cap a four-goal first period and Dale Hawerchuk tallied twice as the Philadelphia Flyers extended their unbeaten streak to 17 games with a 7-3 victory over the Boston Bruins on Tuesday.

Lindros finished with a goal and two assists, while linemate John LeClair had three assists for Philadelphia. Kjell Samuelsson, Daniel Lacroix and Mikael Renberg scored the other goals for the Flyers.
At the Islanders, Jaromir Jagr scored a goal and set up another and Mario Lemieux had three assists in a four-goal second period as the Pittsburgh Penguins beat the New York Islanders 5-3.
Ron Francis, Kevin Hatcher and Petr Nedved also scored in the second period for the Penguins.
Rookie goaltender Patrick Lalime had 47 saves.
In St Louis, Doug Weight scored on a pair of deflections and the Edmonton Oilers spoiled Joel Quenneville's debut as Blues coach with a 5-2 victory over St. Louis.
Miroslav Satan added a goal and two assists and Andrei Kovalenko had a goal and an assist for the Oilers.
Brett Hull scored a goal and set up the other for the Blues.
In Calgary, Dave Gagner scored with 59 seconds left in overtime as the Calgary Flames rallied for a 4-3 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs.
Steve Chiasson unleashed a slap shot from the right point and Gagner deflected it past goaltender Felix Potvin while cutting across the slot for his 12th goal of the season.
German Titov and Jonas Hoglund also scored for the Flames. Jamie Baker scored twice for the Maple Leafs.

In Los Angeles, Ed Olczyk recorded his fifth career hat trick and Vladmir Tsyplakov added a pair of goals as the Los Angeles Kings defeated the Vancouver Canucks for the first time in more than three years, 6-2.
Only 9,548 fans attended the game, the smallest crowd in nine years.

In San Jose, Jeff Friesen's goal with 13:21 left in the third period lifted the San Jose Sharks into a 1-1 tie with the Buffalo Sabres, who received a 42-save game from Steve Shields in his first appearance of the season.
